# notefall

> notefall is a free piano visualizer and MIDI video maker that runs in the browser. Notes fall onto a 3D keyboard, rendered with realistic reflections and textures such as metal, water, ice or glass, and particles drift up from them like smoke. You can record from a MIDI keyboard, edit notes on screen, save as MIDI, and export video up to 4K at 60 fps with no watermark. No account; files are processed locally.

App: https://notefall.app/ (desktop browsers with WebGL, window at least 1024 px wide)

## Look
- Notes are rendered in 3D, with realistic reflections and textures such as metal, water, ice, glass and marble. Light patterns move inside them.
- Particles and soft haze rise from each note and drift like smoke.
- Note shape, color, glow and particles are adjustable. Colors can follow the track, the hand, a gradient across the keyboard, or a random palette; the hit line, particles and key glow use the note's color.
- Keyframes change visual settings during the song.

## Record and edit MIDI
- Record from a MIDI keyboard (Web MIDI), PC keyboard, mouse or touch. Velocity and the sustain pedal are recorded.
- Edit notes on the falling-notes view: add, move, resize, split, delete; velocity, hand and finger per note. Undo and redo.
- Save the song or a recorded take as a MIDI file.

## Export
- 720p, 1080p or 4K; 30 or 60 fps; MP4 (H.264) or WebM (VP9, AV1); WAV for audio only.
- Frames are rendered one by one, so output does not depend on computer speed.

## Other
- Sampled grand piano; timeline with speed changes and an audio track; virtual hands (alpha); projects saved as .nfz files.

## Privacy
MIDI files, recordings, projects and audio never leave the browser. Anonymous usage statistics can be turned off in the app menu.

## Links
- App: https://notefall.app/
- Source: https://github.com/ekkx/notefall
